question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> be a non-negative integer. Then the number of divisors of the form <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> of the number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mn>10</mn></mfenced><mn>10</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mfenced><mn>11</mn></mfenced><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mfenced><mn>13</mn></mfenced><mn>13</mn></msup></math> is equal to _____.

solution.text:
Let N=210×510×1111×1313

Now, power of 2 must be zero,

Power of 5 can be anything,

Power of 13 can be anything.

But, power of 11 should be even.

So, required number of divisors is

1×11×14×6=924.
